passage.text: In 1965, Emma's grandmother, Rose, was nineteen years old.
passage.reading: ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈsɪksti ˈfaɪv, ˈɛməz ˈɡrænmʌðər, ˈroʊz, wʌz ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈjɪrz ˈoʊld.

passage.text: One summer day, she was taking a train from Toronto to Montreal.
passage.reading: ˈwʌn ˈsʌmər ˈdeɪ, ʃiː wʌz ˈteɪkɪŋ ə ˈtreɪn frəm təˈrɑːntoʊ tə ˌmɑːntriˈɔːl.

passage.text: A young man sat down next to her and asked if the seat was free.
passage.reading: ə ˈjʌŋ ˈmæn ˈsæt ˈdaʊn ˈnɛkst tə hɜːr ənd ˈæskt ɪf ðə ˈsiːt wʌz ˈfriː.

passage.text: His name was Jack, and he was going to start a new job in Montreal.
passage.reading: hɪz ˈneɪm wʌz ˈdʒæk, ənd hiː wʌz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ˈstɑːrt ə ˈnuː ˈdʒɑːb ɪn ˌmɑːntriˈɔːl.

passage.text: They talked for five hours, and for Rose, it was love at first sight.
passage.reading: ðeɪ ˈtɔːkt fər ˈfaɪv ˈaʊərz, ənd fər ˈroʊz, ɪt wʌz ˈlʌv ət ˈfɜːrst ˈsaɪt.

passage.text: When the train arrived, Jack asked for her address.
passage.reading: wɛn ðə ˈtreɪn əˈraɪvd, ˈdʒæk ˈæskt fər hɜːr ˈædrɛs.

passage.text: A week later, Rose got his first letter, and she wrote back the same day.
passage.reading: ə ˈwiːk ˈleɪtər, ˈroʊz ˈɡɑːt hɪz ˈfɜːrst ˈlɛtər, ənd ʃiː ˈroʊt ˈbæk ðə ˈseɪm ˈdeɪ.

passage.text: For a year, they wrote to each other every week.
passage.reading: fər ə ˈjɪr, ðeɪ ˈroʊt tu ˈiːtʃ ˈʌðər ˈɛvri ˈwiːk.

passage.text: Jack's letters were full of romance, and Rose kept every one of them.
passage.reading: ˈdʒæks ˈlɛtərz wɜːr ˈfʊl əv roʊˈmæns, ənd ˈroʊz ˈkɛpt ˈɛvri ˈwʌn əv ðɛm.

passage.text: In one letter, Jack wrote, "I want to be with you forever. Will you marry me?"
passage.reading: ɪn ˈwʌn ˈlɛtər, ˈdʒæk ˈroʊt, aɪ ˈwɑːnt tə bi wɪð juː fərˈɛvər. wɪl juː ˈmæri miː?

passage.text: Rose said yes, and they got married in 1966.
passage.reading: ˈroʊz ˈsɛd ˈjɛs, ənd ðeɪ ˈɡɑːt ˈmærid ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈsɪksti ˈsɪks.

passage.text: Sixty years later, they are still crazy about each other.
passage.reading: ˈsɪksti ˈjɪrz ˈleɪtər, ðeɪ ər ˈstɪl ˈkreɪzi əˌbaʊt ˈiːtʃ ˈʌðər.

passage.text: And the letters? They are in a box under their bed, and Emma loves reading them.
passage.reading: ənd ðə ˈlɛtərz? ðeɪ ər ɪn ə ˈbɑːks ˈʌndər ðɛr ˈbɛd, ənd ˈɛmə ˈlʌvz ˈriːdɪŋ ðɛm.
